Not aliens, but death because of excessive heat, lack of clean water, food shortages due to the drought, or in other areas, because of the excessive rains recently.

It's been a lot hotter here in Europe this June. France has said it recorded an increase of more than 2,000 deaths during the last week of a record-breaking European heatwave in June as forecasters warn of further extreme temperatures on the continent in the next few days.

France saw its hottest day ever on average country-wide on 24 June, with temperatures hitting almost 41C (105.8F) in Paris and half the nation placed under a red heat alert. It has been even hotter where I live, further south. 

Deaths in Paris, France, rose 29% in the last week of June compared to the week before, with French health minister Stéphanie Rist adding there had been a "clear increase" in deaths among those over 45. News of the death toll comes with parts of Europe, including the UK, braced for more searing temperatures from this weekend. 


Wildfires are a severe problem just now, too - two weeks ahead of the 'normal season'. 

In Washington DC on 4th July it was 103 (39.4C) and I was deeply relievd that the US weather warning was heeded and the events closed for several hours! I'm worried for friends in the US who are currently surrounded by wild fires. 

So, not aliens, but weather related problems and wildfires are the most likely culprits for  you in the US, too...
